newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Fire in Jakarta leaves 2,000 homeless, no deaths.
newsitem.headline: Fire in Jakarta leaves 2,000 homeless, no deaths.

text.p: Fire raged through a poor residential district in the Indonesian capital Jakarta on Monday, leaving around 2,000 people homeless but causing no deaths or serious injuries, witnesses said.
A local official from the district of Karet Tengsin said the fire, which burned for more than two hours before being put out by fire fighters, ravaged about 300 homes in the densely populated area.
Police and residents said there were no immediate reports of deaths or serious injuries.
Witnesses said hundreds of residents fled with their possessions as the fire advanced. Many took furniture, valuables and motorcycles to a nearby sports field.
More than a dozen fire engines had rushed to the scene.
Residents said the fire started in a small restaurant by the side of a canal after an accident with a cooking stove, but police said they were still investigating the incident.
A column of black smoke from the blaze could be seen from many parts of the capital.
Fires often break out in Jakarta because of the widespread practice in many low-income homes of storing petrol and other fuels within the premises.
However, many fires are also blamed on unscrupulous developers trying to clear the urban poor from valuable land for redevelopment as office and high rise residential apartments.
